questions.ask: Could you tell me your postcode, please?
Could you tell me the last four digits of your account number, please?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions financial hardship: job loss, illness, bereavement, being unable to afford essentials.
intents.dispute: The customer says "This is not my debt" or "I never had this product".
intents.already_paid: The customer says "I have already paid".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments.
intents.vague: The customer gives a vague time, e.g. "soon", "after payday".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.
intents.human: The customer asks for a human.

lines.opening: Good day, this is Isla, Corran Bank's automated assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: To check, please call the number on the back of your card.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only explain once I know I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details until I have confirmed your identity.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back on a business day, today or in the next two business days, between half past nine in the morning and six in the evening. Could you suggest another time?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {first_name} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we continue, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_explain: I can only continue once I have confirmed your identity, and these questions protect your account.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity. Please call the number on the back of your card or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I am calling about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record that amount. The lowest amount I can record is {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't record that amount.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, the date must be today or later. Which date would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next date I can record is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay on {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Could you give me an exact date?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_item: For your {name}, you will pay {amount} on {date}.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can record is {date}.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a confirmation by text message.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, because of a system problem your promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear you are going through this. I will put you through to our care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I will put you through to a colleague who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: Can I help you with anything first?
lines.transfer: I am transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change the promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.

assumptions: Currency is pounds: the get_account fields past_due, minimum_due and monthly_instalment are described as pounds.

amount_scale is 100 because create_promise wants the amount in pence as a whole number (brief rule 32 and the API). get_account returns amounts in pounds, not pence. The engine converts pounds to pence for create_promise only, e.g. £85.50 becomes 8550.

The brief prescribes 'This call is recorded.' in the opening. The spec format forbids that passive wording and the word 'recorded' outside the promise lines, so the opening says 'We record this call.' The meaning is the same.
The confirm question uses the brief's words 'Is this {first_name} {last_name}?'. No title is given. Rule 2 allows one more ask, so max_asks is 2.

Callback: today or one of the next two business days, business days only, 09:30 to 18:00 with both ends included, and later than now (rule 5). One more ask is allowed after the first bad slot, so max_asks is 2 (rule 6).

Identity: postcode first, then account_last4 (rule 9). The postcode is sent in capitals with every space removed, so no format is set. Postcode length varies, so no length is set. account_last4 is exactly 4 digits with leading zeros kept (rule 10 and the API).
max_wrong is 2, counted across both questions (rule 11 and the API summary).

The verify_identity response has no hint field (its fields are ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left and all_verified). So response.hint is empty and hints is empty. No dates are asked, so date_order keeps the default dmy (UK bank).

purpose_is_decline keeps the default true. The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining. Rule 12: the agent says once that the questions protect the account, and a second refusal declines identity.
The floor is minimum_due for credit_card and overdraft, and monthly_instalment for personal_loan, capped at past_due (rule 22). floor_names come from the field meanings.

Bands come from the rule 16 table. Early: the 8th business day after today (rule 17). Middle: today + 14 calendar days, moved FORWARD to the next business day if that day is not one (rule 18), hence deadline_adjust next_business_day. Late: the last calendar day of the current month, moved BACK to the last business day; if that is before today, the last business day of next month is used (rule 19). The last_business_day_of_month kind is assumed to handle this, including the move to next month.

Middle and late bands differ at attempt 2, so each band has its own ladder. Attempt 1 is past_due on the next business day, or the deadline if that is earlier (the engine clamps to the deadline). Middle attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline. Late attempts 2 and 3 are past_due on the deadline, then the floor on the deadline. The top-level ladder repeats the late ladder.

Proposals that would use past_due are full_or_floor, because after 'too much' every proposal uses the floor instead of past_due (rule 24). A proposal that repeats an earlier one exactly is skipped and the customer is not asked again (rule 27).
too_much_floor is asked_date: the floor is offered once on the date of the current proposal and uses no attempt (rule 24).
first_ask is 'today', with the exact words 'Can you pay the full amount today?' (rule 25). It is not an attempt.
No rule is given for days_late outside 1 to 60. The brief only calls customers who are 1 to 60 days late, so bands_outside is null.
A vague date that stays vague after one more ask is a flat refusal (rule 21), so refuse_deadline_is_refusal keeps its default true.
Notes are enabled: the closing table gives note reasons for already paid, refused, dispute and system failure. The note goes in just before close_call. No note is written for transfers.

Hardship transfers straight to the care queue with reason hardship and makes no offer (rule 37). The hardship and transfer_support events are therefore the same, and the hardship line says the transfer is happening.
A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments transfers to payment_plans (rule 38). A human request transfers to customer_service after one offer of help (rule 39).
The brief does not say what 'next <weekday>' means. The default following_week is used.
The brief does not limit 'I don't want to talk'. The default max_not_talk 2 is used.
The brief does not say whether to ask 'anything else' after a promise. The default true is used.
The brief has no rule for changing a recorded promise, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
The scam reply uses the brief's words: call the number on the back of the card (rule 40).
The multi settings keep their defaults. Each call has exactly one product, so they have no effect.
get_account returns the product as the single object 'product', not an array. list_field is 'product', id_field is 'product_id' and type_field is 'type'.
The add_note 'text' field and the close_call 'reason' field are optional in the API, so they are not mapped as constants. The reason is sent from the event when the event has one.
